message.content:
You are writing a concrete EXECUTION PLAN for a secondary-income business for Hooman (Adobe eng manager; $25-150K capital; ~10-20 hrs/wk alongside a day job; wants $5-30K/mo; already building CutLog).

IDEA: "Managed technical hosting / DevOps-lite subscription (HostiFi model)"

The deep-research/validation stage produced these findings (JSON) — BUILD THE PLAN AROUND THE VALIDATED REALITY, not the original optimistic pitch:
{
  "idea": "Managed technical hosting / DevOps-lite subscription (HostiFi model): pick one popular self-hosted tool with a large non-technical install base, build provisioning + monitoring + billing automation, sell flat $10-50/mo/instance recurring.",
  "slug": "managed_hosting",
  "assumptions_checked": [
    {
      "claim": "Reilly Chase bootstrapped HostiFi solo to $100K/yr then ~$1M ARR (then acquired/exited).",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "Revenue path VERIFIED and understated: HostiFi hit $10K MRR (~$120K ARR) in ~8 months of a 2019 bootstrapped launch, reached $1M ARR ~1yr early (~2021), now does $3M+/yr (some sources $7M+) with 3,000+ customers. Founder was non-technical at start, sold his house to fund it, no TinySeed funding (absent from tinyseed.com/portfolio) = bootstrapped confirmed. BUT the 'exited/acquired' framing is FALSE: Chase is still CEO and HostiFi is the acquirer (acquired SimpleFly Tech). Sources: hostifi.com, ownerpreneur.com, theorg.com/org/hostifi, crunchbase.com/organization/hostifi, hostifi.com/simplefly."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Infra IS the product = 1:1 fit with Hooman's Adobe cloud/infra skills.",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "The actual work (provisioning DO VMs, Zabbix monitoring, Backblaze/DO Spaces backups, Let's Encrypt SSL, migrations across 32 DCs) is exactly cloud/infra/systems work, so the BUILD fit is real (hostifi.com features). BUT HostiFi's founder was NON-technical; growth came from early community position + sales/support, i.e. Hooman's flagged distribution weakness. The fit is on the wrong axis: the infra was never the bottleneck."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Most AI-safe / boring / low-competition.",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "AI-safe TRUE (uptime/hosting isn't LLM-disintermediated). Low-competition FALSE: a horizontal 'managed self-hosted app' layer already exists and is racing pricing down — Elestio (400+ apps, from $11/mo), PikaPods (from $1.80/mo), Cloudron (EUR15-25/mo), Sliplane, plus DO/AWS 1-click marketplaces. Sources: elest.io/pricing, pikapods.com, cloudron.io/pricing."
    },
    {
      "claim": "$5-25K/mo profit realistic.",
      "status": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence": "HostiFi proves the ceiling exists but as a 6+yr outlier with a team. For a part-time solo operator in yr 1-2, netting $5K/mo needs ~100-300 paid instances at $19-99/mo after cloud COGS and churn — a real sales grind in a fragmented base. Realistic base case discounted to $2-8K/mo in 12-24mo; $10-25K is a multi-year outcome."
    },
    {
      "claim": "~$25-60K capital, largely bootstrappable from client cash.",
      "status": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "No inventory/debt/PG; capital is cloud float + tooling + some ads. HostiFi literally bootstrapped from client cash. If anything <$25K is achievable, so the number improves in the idea's favor."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Lowest downside in the set.",
      "status": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Worst case = lost time + a few $K infra spend. No inventory/debt/personal-guarantee. Consistent with master report section 5."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Open question: which self-hosted tool has a large non-technical base AND does NOT compete with the vendor's own cloud? / Risk of vendor launching own cloud.",
      "status": "FALSE",
      "evidence": "The clean niche barely exists. UniFi (best-proven) is double-covered: HostiFi incumbency PLUS Ubiquiti's OWN 'Official UniFi Hosting'/Site Manager launched ~2022 (help.ui.com article 4415364143511) — the exact vendor-cloud risk, already materialized. n8n is license-gated (Sustainable Use License limits use to 'own internal business purposes', distribution only 'free of charge for non-commercial purposes'; commercial hosting needs a separate n8n license) AND has n8n Cloud. Ghost/WordPress saturated/vendor-owned. Remaining OSS tools skew developer (technical base, breaks thesis) or hobbyist (PikaPods $1.80/mo floor). Untaken niches have NO proof point."
    }
  ],
  "competitors": [
    "HostiFi — incumbent, $19/$99/$249/mo tiers (25/250/1000 devices), 3,000+ customers, $3M+/yr (some sources $7M+), bootstrapped, owns UniFi/UISP/Omada community",
    "Ubiquiti Official UniFi Hosting / Site Manager — the VENDOR's own managed cloud, low-cost/near-free per site, launched ~2022, structural competitor to any UniFi host",
    "Elestio (elest.io) — 400+ managed open-source apps (n8n, Supabase, Keycloak, Postgres), from $11/mo + $0.15/GB, L2 support $50/L3 $200, multi-cloud",
    "PikaPods (pikapods.com) — resource-priced from $1.80/mo, hosts n8n/Immich/Actual; the price floor",
    "Cloudron (cloudron.io) — self-hosting platform, Free (2 apps)/Pro EUR15/Max EUR25 per month",
    "Sliplane, Coolify-as-a-service, DigitalOcean & AWS 1-click marketplaces — additional low-cost commoditizers of one-click OSS deploy",
    "n8n Cloud — first-party managed hosting for n8n, disqualifying n8n as a third-party target"
  ],
  "economics_verified": "Capital IMPROVED vs pitch: realistically <$25K (vs pitched $25-60K), bootstrappable from client cash, no debt/inventory/PG. Margin ~60-80% after real cloud COGS (VMs, Backblaze/DO Spaces backups, Zabbix) — high, confirmed. Revenue HALVED vs pitch: realistic $2-8K/mo in 12-24mo (vs pitched $5-25K); $5K/mo needs ~100-300 paid instances; $10-25K/mo is a multi-year outlier. Ramp is SLOW — the bottleneck is community/sales grind, not the build. Downside confirmed lowest in the set (time + a few $K). Net: capital/downside better than pitched; income and ramp worse; and the moat is distribution/community, not infra — inverting the founder-fit story.",
  "verdict": "CONDITIONAL",
  "confidence": "MEDIUM",
  "kill_risks": [
    "Vendor launches (or already runs) its own managed cloud — CONFIRMED for UniFi (~2022) and n8n; this is the base rate for any successful self-hosted tool, not a tail risk",
    "License prohibits commercial reselling — n8n's Sustainable Use License blocks hosting-as-a-service without a paid commercial license; many modern OSS tools (SSPL/BSL/fair-source) do the same",
    "No proven niche left — the untaken targets have NO proof point, so the #1 Track-B filter (proven playbook) fails exactly where competition is low",
    "Distribution/community grind is Hooman's flagged weakness AND a second 0->1 front competing with CutLog for his scarce ~10-20 hrs/wk — the exact trap master report section 5 warns against",
    "Horizontal price floor already set at $1.80-$11/mo by funded incumbents (PikaPods, Elestio), below the pitch's $10-50 assumption",
    "24/7 uptime/on-call obligation makes it not cleanly part-time unless a contractor is hired early, which thins margin"
  ],
  "best_niche_or_target": "There is NO clean best target as pitched. The best-PROVEN niche (Ubiquiti UniFi/UISP/Omada network controllers, large non-technical SMB/MSP/WISP base) is disqualified for a newcomer: double-covered by incumbent HostiFi AND Ubiquiti's own Official UniFi Hosting since ~2022. The next-obvious (n8n) is license-gated + has n8n Cloud. The only CONDITIONAL path is a specific niche B2B self-hosted tool with (a) a real non-technical PAYING base, (b) no first-party cloud, and (c) a permissive license — but no such target currently has a proof point, which is why it fails the Track-B 'proven playbook' bar. Practical recommendation: do not build this from scratch; if pursuing the shape at all, validate a specific under-covered niche tool's paid demand BEFORE building, and prefer deploying capital into a cash-flowing acquisition over opening a second distribution front against CutLog.",
  "_idea": {
    "slug": "managed_hosting",
    "name": "Managed technical hosting / DevOps-lite subscription (HostiFi model)",
    "claims": "Infra IS the product = 1:1 fit with Hooman Adobe cloud/infra skills; most AI-safe; $5-25K/mo; ~$25-60K capital, largely bootstrappable from client cash; low downside. Proof: Reilly Chase bootstrapped HostiFi solo to $100K/yr then ~$1M ARR. Key open questions: which self-hosted tool has a large NON-technical base AND does NOT compete with the vendor own managed cloud? Risk of vendor launching their own cloud?"
  }
}

Also read your own research doc at /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/trackB/deep/managed_hosting/01_research_validation.md for detail.

Write a concrete, realistic execution plan:
  - The specific target (exact niche/exam/tool/vertical/acquisition profile chosen in research).
  - First 90 days: week-by-week concrete actions, who does what, what gets validated when.
  - Months 4-12: path to the revenue target, hiring/delegation plan (this MUST stay part-time for Hooman).
  - Itemized budget within $25-150K; monthly burn; break-even point.
  - Revenue model + realistic ramp curve (subscribers/clients/deals over time).
  - Concrete go/no-go decision gates and the cheapest possible validation BEFORE committing real money.
  - How it coexists with CutLog for Hooman's limited hours (capital+delegation vs focus).

WRITE the plan to /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/trackB/deep/managed_hosting/02_execution_plan.md (use Write). Return a ~200-word summary of the plan as your final text.

1	# Deep Research + Skeptic Validation — Managed Technical Hosting / DevOps-lite (HostiFi model)
2	
3	**Date**: 2026-07-01. **Analyst**: Claude (Opus 4.8), Track-B skeptic pass.
4	**Idea (from TRACKB_REPORT.md #2, score 8.4)**: pick one popular self-hosted tool with a large
5	non-technical install base, build provisioning + monitoring + billing automation, sell flat
6	$10–50/mo/instance recurring. Pitch says: infra IS the product (1:1 fit with Hooman's Adobe
7	cloud/infra skills), most AI-safe, $5–25K/mo, ~$25–60K capital largely bootstrappable from
8	client cash, lowest downside. Proof: Reilly Chase bootstrapped HostiFi solo to $100K/yr then ~$1M ARR.
9	
10	**Verdict up front: CONDITIONAL (leaning PASS as pitched). Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH.**
11	The proof point is REAL and the founder-fit is genuine, but the two open questions in the pitch
12	turn out to be the two things that break it: (1) the single best-proven target (UniFi) already
13	has the vendor's own cloud competing head-on since ~2022, and (2) the other "obvious" targets
14	(n8n and most modern self-hosted tools) either license-prohibit reselling or already have a
15	first-party managed cloud. The clean "large non-technical base AND no vendor cloud" niche the
16	pitch asks for is largely already taken. See §3.
17	
18	---
19	
20	## 1. Claim-by-claim verification
21	
22	### Claim A — "Reilly Chase bootstrapped HostiFi solo to $100K/yr then ~$1M ARR." → **VERIFIED (and understated)**
23	- HostiFi hit **$10K MRR ($120K ARR) within ~8 months** of a 2019 bootstrapped launch, and
24	  reached **$1M ARR ~a year ahead of a Sept-2022 goal** (i.e. ~2021). Today it does
25	  **>$3M annual revenue serving 3,000+ customers globally.** Some sources cite $7M+ revenue.
26	  (ownerpreneur.com summary via search; theorg.com/org/hostifi; crunchbase.com/organization/hostifi.)
27	- Founder **Reilly Chase** was **non-technical at the start** (learned WordPress + Python
28	  scripting), started **after being fired in Jan 2019**, and **sold his house** to fund it when
29	  MRR was below his mortgage. (ownerpreneur.com / blog.hostifi.com.)
30	- **Bootstrapped confirmed**: HostiFi is **NOT** in the TinySeed portfolio (tinyseed.com/portfolio
31	  checked — no HostiFi / Reilly Chase entry), consistent with the bootstrapped narrative.
32	- **Correction to pitch language**: the pitch implies "then acquired/exited." That is **FALSE as
33	  stated** — Chase is **still CEO** and HostiFi has itself been the **acquirer** (e.g. SimpleFly
34	  Tech "acquired by HostiFi", per hostifi.com/simplefly). No exit. This doesn't hurt the thesis
35	  (it's a bigger, still-growing business than "$1M then sold"), but the pitch's fact is wrong.
36	
37	### Claim B — "Infra IS the product → 1:1 fit with Hooman's cloud/infra skills." → **VERIFIED (directionally true, with an asterisk)**
38	- The work HostiFi actually does — provisioning cloud VMs (DigitalOcean), monitoring (Zabbix),
39	  nightly backups (DO Spaces + Backblaze B2), SSL (Let's Encrypt), 32 data centers, migrations —
40	  is exactly cloud/infra/systems work. (hostifi.com pricing/features page.) So the *technical*
41	  fit is real.
42	- **Asterisk**: HostiFi's growth was **NOT driven by the founder's infra skill** — Chase was
43	  non-technical. It was driven by **being early to a specific vendor community (Ubiquiti/UniFi)
44	  and by sales/support/ops**, i.e. the exact **distribution muscle Hooman lacks** and that this
45	  whole Track-B study flags as his one weakness (final_report §3). So "1:1 skills fit" is true
46	  for the *build*, but the build was never the bottleneck. This is the central tension.
47	
48	### Claim C — "Most AI-safe / boring." → **PARTIALLY TRUE**
49	- Hosting/uptime of a specific vendor's controller is not something an LLM disintermediates, so
50	  it's AI-safe in the "content gets commoditized" sense. TRUE.
51	- But it is **NOT low-competition or un-crowded**. A whole layer of horizontal "managed
52	  self-hosted app" companies already exists and is **racing pricing to the floor** (see §2):
53	  Elestio (400+ apps, from $11/mo), PikaPods (from **$1.80/mo**), Cloudron, Sliplane, plus
54	  DigitalOcean/AWS 1-click marketplaces. The moat is community position, not technology.
55	
56	### Claim D — "$5–25K/mo profit." → **UNVERIFIED / optimistic at the top end; plausible at the low end**
57	- HostiFi proves the *ceiling* exists ($3M+/yr) — but that's the survivorship outlier after
58	  6+ years and a team. For a **part-time solo operator in year 1–2**, the realistic figure is
59	  the **bottom of the range or below**. To net $5K/mo at $19–99/mo plans you need roughly
60	  **100–300 paying instances** after cloud-cost COGS and churn — that's a real sales grind in a
61	  fragmented buyer base, not a "build it and they come." $10–25K/mo is a multi-year outcome, not
62	  a base case. Mark the income claim **discounted to $2–8K/mo realistic in 12–24mo**.
63	
64	### Claim E — "~$25–60K capital, largely bootstrappable from client cash." → **VERIFIED**
65	- No inventory, no debt, no PG. Capital is cloud float + tooling + ~some ads. HostiFi literally
66	  bootstrapped from client cash. This is the strongest, most-defensible claim in the pitch.
67	  Realistic capital to start is arguably **<$25K** — the $25–60K is conservative. **VERIFIED, and if anything the number improves in the idea's favor.**
68	
69	### Claim F — "Lowest downside in the set." → **VERIFIED**
70	- Worst case = lost time + a few $K of infra spend. No inventory/debt/PG. Consistent with §5 of
71	  the master report. **VERIFIED.**
72	
73	### Claim G (open question) — "Risk of vendor launching their own cloud?" → **CONFIRMED, ALREADY HAPPENED**
74	- **Ubiquiti launched its own "Official UniFi Hosting"** (help.ui.com/hc/en-us/articles/
75	  4415364143511 — "hosted and maintained by us in the cloud," ~2022), plus **UniFi Site Manager
76	  / Cloud Console** remote management. This is the **exact tail risk the pitch names, and it has
77	  already materialized for the single best-proven target.** HostiFi survived by moving upmarket
78	  (MSPs/WISPs, UISP/ISP platform, migrations, phone support, compliance docs, SSH, custom
79	  firewall — things the bare vendor cloud doesn't do) and by first-mover community lock-in — NOT
80	  by being cheaper. A new solo entrant on UniFi today faces both HostiFi AND Ubiquiti's own free/
81	  cheap cloud. **This effectively kills UniFi as the entry niche for a newcomer.**
82	
83	---
84	
85	## 2. Real competitors (named, with pricing/scale)
86	
87	**Vertical (UniFi/network) — the proven vein, but taken:**
88	- **HostiFi** — the incumbent. $19/mo (25 devices) → $99 (250) → $249 (1,000) → custom.
89	  >3,000 customers, $3M+/yr (some sources $7M+). Owns the UniFi/UISP/Omada community. (hostifi.com)
90	- **Ubiquiti "Official UniFi Hosting" / Site Manager** — the **vendor's own** managed cloud,
91	  low-cost/near-free per site, launched ~2022. Structural competitor to any UniFi host.
92	  (help.ui.com article 4415364143511.)
93	
94	**Horizontal (managed self-hosted apps) — crowded and price-collapsing:**
95	- **Elestio** (elest.io) — **400+ open-source apps** (n8n, WordPress, Supabase, Keycloak,
96	  Postgres…), managed VMs from **$11/mo** + $0.15/GB storage, L2 support $50, L3 $200. Multi-cloud.
97	- **PikaPods** (pikapods.com) — resource-priced from **$1.80/mo**, hosts n8n, Immich, Actual,
98	  etc. This is the price floor.
99	- **Cloudron** (cloudron.io) — self-hosting *platform* (you run the server), Free (2 apps) /
100	  Pro €15/mo / Max €25/mo. Competes for the "make self-hosting easy" job.
101	- **Sliplane / Coolify-as-a-service / DigitalOcean & AWS 1-click marketplaces** — additional
102	  low-cost commoditizers of the "one-click deploy an open-source app" job.
103	
104	**Read**: The vertical version (one vendor community) is the only defensible shape — but the best
105	one (UniFi) is owned by HostiFi + the vendor. The horizontal version is already a price war
106	between funded/established players charging $1.80–$11/mo, i.e. below the pitch's $10–50 assumption.
107	
108	---
109	
110	## 3. The specific-niche question — "large NON-technical base AND no vendor cloud"
111	
112	This is the crux of the pitch, and real data says the clean answer barely exists:
113	
114	| Candidate target | Non-technical base? | Vendor's own cloud? | Reseller-friendly license? | Verdict |
115	|---|---|---|---|---|
116	| **UniFi / UISP / Omada** | Yes (huge) | **YES — Ubiquiti Official Hosting (~2022)** | n/a | **Taken** (HostiFi + vendor) |
117	| **n8n** | Growing | **YES — n8n Cloud** | **NO** — Sustainable Use License limits use to "your own internal business purposes"; distribution only "free of charge for non-commercial purposes"; hosting-as-a-service needs a **separate commercial/OEM license from n8n** (docs.n8n.io; LICENSE.md). | **Legally gated** |
118	| **Ghost / Discourse / WordPress** | Yes | **YES — Ghost(Pro), first-party** for Ghost; WP is infinitely hosted (commodity) | Mixed | **Saturated / vendor-owned** |
119	| **Supabase / Keycloak / Postgres** | **No** (developer tools) | Often yes | OSS-friendly | Base is technical → violates the thesis |
120	| **Immich / Actual / self-host homelab apps** | Somewhat | Usually no | OSS-friendly | Base skews hobbyist/low-willingness-to-pay; PikaPods already at $1.80/mo |
121	| **Status pages / uptime / small niche B2B tools** | Maybe | Varies | Varies | **Unproven** — this is where a real gap *might* still exist, but there is NO proof point |
122

128	the "clear proven path" that is the #1 Track-B filter evaporates for the untaken niches.
129	
130	---
131	
132	## 4. Re-derived realistic economics
133	
134	| Metric | Pitch | Re-derived (skeptic) | What changed |
135	|---|---|---|---|
136	| Revenue/mo | $5–25K | **$2–8K in 12–24mo; $5K+ requires ~100–300 paid instances** | Halved the base case; top end is a multi-year outlier |

143	Net: capital and downside are **better** than pitched; income and ramp are **worse/slower**; and
144	the moat is a distribution/community moat, not an infra moat — which inverts the founder-fit story.

146	---
147	
148	## 5. Kill-risks
149	
150	1. **Vendor launches (or already runs) its own managed cloud** — CONFIRMED for UniFi (~2022) and

165	## 6. Verdict
166	
167	**CONDITIONAL, leaning PASS as pitched. Confidence MEDIUM-HIGH.**
168	
169	- The **proof point is real and strong** (HostiFi $3M+, bootstrapped, non-technical founder),

# Execution Plan — Managed Technical Hosting / DevOps-lite (HostiFi model)

**Date**: 2026-07-01. **Author**: Claude (Opus 4.8). **For**: Hooman Shariati.
**Companion doc**: `01_research_validation.md` (read it first — this plan is built on its
CONDITIONAL verdict, not the original optimistic pitch).

---

## 0. The one thing to internalize before spending a dollar

Research verdict = **CONDITIONAL, MEDIUM confidence.** The proof point (HostiFi) is real, the
capital/downside are the best in the whole idea set, and the *build* is 1:1 with Hooman's infra
skills. **But three findings invert the pitch:**

1. **The infra was never the bottleneck.** HostiFi's founder was non-technical; the moat was
   community position + sales/support — exactly Hooman's flagged weakness.
2. **No clean target exists.** UniFi is double-covered (HostiFi incumbency **+** Ubiquiti's own
   Official Hosting since ~2022). n8n is license-gated + has n8n Cloud. Horizontal players
   (Elestio $11/mo, PikaPods $1.80/mo) already set the price floor below the pitch's $10–50.
3. **It's a second 0→1 distribution front** competing with CutLog for the same scarce 10–20 hrs/wk.

**Consequence:** this plan is deliberately **gated and validation-first**. We spend real build
money **only after** a paying-demand signal, and we present the **acquisition path as the
recommended default** because it is the only variant that (a) sidesteps the distribution grind,
(b) keeps Hooman part-time via inherited ops, and (c) matches the research's explicit
recommendation ("deploy capital into a cash-flowing acquisition over opening a second
distribution front"). We do **not** build a from-scratch UniFi/n8n host. Full stop.

**Revenue framing for the whole plan:** realistic **$2–8K/mo net in 12–24 months**; $5K/mo needs
~100–300 paid instances; $10–25K/mo is a multi-year outlier. Plan to the base case, not the pitch.

---

## 1. The specific target (chosen)

The research proves there is **no clean greenfield niche**, so we split into two mutually-exclusive
tracks and pick between them at Gate 1 (Day 30). Hooman does NOT run both.

### Track A (RECOMMENDED default) — Acquire a small, cash-flowing managed-hosting micro-SaaS
- **Profile to buy:** a single-tool managed-hosting business doing **$3–12K/mo MRR**, **>60% margin**,
  **<15 hrs/wk owner involvement**, **>18 months operating history**, **<5% monthly churn**, on a
  tool with **no aggressive first-party cloud** and a **permissive license**.
- **Where:** Acquire.com (formerly MicroAcquire), Flippa (SaaS filter), Tiny Acquisitions,
  IndieHackers "for sale", MicroConf/founder Slacks, direct outreach to sub-scale hosts.
- **Price band:** $25–120K (roughly **2.5–4× annual profit** for a part-time-run micro-SaaS).
  Fits the $25–150K envelope with headroom for transition costs.
- **Why this over building:** you buy the customer base + community position + proven playbook —
  the exact things the research says can't be built from scratch part-time. Infra skills become a
  **margin/reliability edge** (improve provisioning, cut COGS, reduce on-call), which is the
  correct axis for Hooman's strengths.

### Track B (FALLBACK, only if Gate 1 finds a validated niche) — Build one narrow niche host
- **Target profile (all four must hold):** (1) a **specific B2B self-hosted tool** with a real
  **non-technical paying base**; (2) **no first-party managed cloud**; (3) a **permissive license**
  (MIT/Apache/GPL — NOT SSPL/BSL/Fair-source/Sustainable-Use); (4) a reachable community with
  evidence of willingness to pay ≥ $25/mo.
- **Explicitly disqualified:** UniFi/UISP/Omada (taken), n8n (license + n8n Cloud), Ghost/WordPress
  (saturated/vendor-owned), developer tools (technical base), homelab/hobbyist apps (PikaPods
  $1.80/mo floor).
- **Candidate hunting ground (unproven, to be validated, not assumed):** niche vertical B2B
  self-hosted tools — e.g. self-hosted booking/scheduling, small-clinic/practice tools, church/
  nonprofit management, self-hosted LMS for training companies, self-hosted helpdesk for MSPs.
  **None has a proof point** — that is precisely what Gate 1 must produce before any build spend.

---

## 2. First 90 days — week by week

Budget for the whole 90 days: **≤ $2,000** (all validation; no product build until Gate 2).
Time: **≤ 6 hrs/wk** so CutLog keeps priority. "Hooman" = does it himself; "Contractor" not yet hired.

### Weeks 1–2 — Market & deal-flow scan (both tracks in parallel, cheap)
- **Hooman:** Create buyer accounts on Acquire.com, Flippa, Tiny Acquisitions. Set saved searches
  ("managed hosting", "self-hosted", "SaaS", MRR $2–12K). Log every listing matching Track-A
  profile into a sheet with MRR, margin, tool, license, churn, ask price, owner hrs/wk.
- **Hooman:** Build the "disqualifier checklist" (vendor cloud? license? technical base?) and run
  the top 20 candidate self-hosted tools through it for Track B. Kill fast.
- **Validated by end of Wk2:** Is there ≥1 credible Track-A acquisition candidate AND/OR ≥1
  Track-B tool passing all four filters? If **zero on both** → early NO-GO (see Gate 0).

### Weeks 3–4 — Demand probes (Track B) + first seller conversations (Track A)
- **Track A / Hooman:** Contact 3–5 sellers. Ask for MRR proof (Stripe screenshots), churn,
  COGS, support-ticket volume, on-call load, license status of hosted tool, concentration risk.
- **Track B / Hooman:** For each surviving tool, post/DM in its community: "Would you pay $X/mo to
  never touch the server?" Target **10 qualitative replies** and **≥3 "yes, take my money now"**.
  Optionally stand up a $5 landing page (Carrd) + Stripe "pre-order" link — **a real card charge
  is the only signal that counts.**
- **Validated by end of Wk4:** Track A — at least one seller with verifiable Stripe MRR and clean
  license/vendor-cloud story. Track B — ≥3 real pre-commitments (card or signed LOI).

### Gate 1 (Day 30) — PICK ONE TRACK OR STOP
- **Go Track A** if: a candidate with verified MRR ≥ $3K/mo, margin ≥ 60%, churn < 5%/mo, owner
  hrs < 15/wk, clean license/no-vendor-cloud, ask ≤ 4× profit.
- **Go Track B** if: ≥3 paying pre-commitments on a tool passing all four filters AND no
  acceptable Track-A deal exists.
- **STOP** if neither. Sunk cost so far ≤ ~$500 + ~24 hrs. This is the whole point of gating.

### Weeks 5–8 — Diligence (Track A) OR MVP scoping (Track B)
- **Track A / Hooman + hired advisor:** Deep diligence on the chosen deal — verify Stripe payouts
  vs claimed MRR, cohort churn, refund rate, hosting-COGS invoices, customer concentration, TOS/
  license of the hosted tool, transferability of infra + domains + support inbox. Engage an
  **escrow (Escrow.com) + a lightweight SaaS-purchase-agreement template** (lawyer review, ~$1.5K).
- **Track B / Hooman:** Scope the thinnest possible provisioning+billing+monitoring MVP for the
  one validated tool. Reuse the CutLog stack where possible (Vercel/Stripe patterns already known).

### Weeks 9–12 — Close (Track A) OR ship private beta (Track B)
- **Track A / Hooman:** Close via escrow. Run a **30-day transition** with the seller retained on
  a handover retainer (support SOPs, on-call runbook, community access). **Do not change pricing
  or stack in month 1** — just keep the lights on and observe.
- **Track B / Hooman:** Ship to the ≥3 pre-committed customers. Charge real money day one.
- **Gate 2 (Day 90):** Track A — MRR held within 5% of purchase through transition, on-call load
  confirmed < 8 hrs/wk. Track B — ≥5 paying instances live, churn signal acceptable. Else pause.

---

## 3. Months 4–12 — path to revenue, staying part-time

**Non-negotiable constraint:** Hooman stays ≤ 10 hrs/wk on this and CutLog remains his primary
0→1. The lever that keeps this part-time is **delegation of ops/support/on-call**, funded by the
business's own margin. If it can't fund its own contractor, it isn't working — pause it.

### Track A (acquisition) 12-month path
- **Month 4:** Hire a **part-time ops/support contractor** ($1.5–3K/mo, offshore or fractional)
  to own tier-1 support + on-call rotation. Hooman = architecture, COGS optimization, escalations.
- **Months 5–7:** Apply infra edge — migrate to cheaper/more-reliable provisioning, automate the
  top 3 manual support tasks, tighten backups/monitoring. Goal: **lift margin 5–10 pts** and cut
  Hooman's own hours toward < 5/wk.
- **Months 8–12:** Grow via the inherited community position (SEO, existing customer referrals,
  one adjacent tool if it passes the same 4 filters). Target **+30–50% MRR** organically.
- **12-mo target:** if bought at $5K/mo MRR → **$6.5–8K/mo MRR, ~$4–6K/mo net** after contractor
  and COGS. Within the realistic base case.

### Track B (build) 12-month path — slower, harder, only if Gate 1 forced it
- **Months 4–6:** Grind the one community that pre-committed. Content + direct outreach. Target
  **20–40 paid instances**.
- **Month 6:** Hire the support/on-call contractor **the moment MRR clears ~$3K/mo** — do not let
  on-call trap Hooman full-time.
- **Months 7–12:** Reach **60–100 paid instances** = ~$2–5K/mo net at $25–50/mo. This is a slog and
  the honest ceiling for a part-time year-1 build; if it stalls under 30 instances by month 9,
  **cut it** and redirect hours to CutLog.

---

## 4. Budget (within $25–150K), burn, break-even

### Track A (recommended)
| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Acquisition price (2.5–4× profit; target ~$5K/mo MRR biz) | $40–100K |
| Legal (SaaS purchase agreement review) + escrow fees | $2–3K |
| Seller transition retainer (1 month) | $2–4K |
| Cloud/tooling float during transition | $1–2K |
| **Upfront total** | **$45–109K** |
| Ongoing monthly burn (contractor + cloud COGS) | **$2.5–5K/mo** |
| **Break-even** | If acquired cash-flow-positive, **immediate** on operating basis; recover purchase price in **~18–30 months** at base-case net |

### Track B (fallback)
| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Validation (Weeks 1–4) | $0.5–2K |
| Build (reuse CutLog stack) | $3–6K |
| Cloud float + tooling (yr 1) | $3–5K |
| Support contractor (from ~month 6, funded by MRR) | $1.5–3K/mo |
| **Upfront before contractor** | **~$8–13K** |
| **Break-even** | ~**60–80 paid instances** (~$2–3K/mo net) covering contractor + COGS; realistically **month 9–15** |

Both tracks sit comfortably inside the $25–150K envelope. Track A uses more capital (the point:
**capital substitutes for the distribution grind Hooman can't do part-time**). Track B is cheaper
but pays for it in Hooman's scarcest resource — hours.

---

## 5. Revenue model + realistic ramp

- **Model:** flat recurring $19–99/mo per instance (Track A inherits its own tiers; Track B
  targets $25–50/mo — never compete at the $1.80–$11 horizontal floor).
- **Margin:** 60–80% after cloud COGS (VMs, Backblaze/DO Spaces backups, Zabbix). Confirmed.

**Ramp (Track A, base case, bought at ~$5K/mo MRR):**
| Month | 3 | 6 | 9 | 12 | 18 | 24 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MRR | 5.0K | 5.5K | 6.2K | 7.0K | 8.5K | 10K |
| Net after contractor+COGS | ~1.5K | ~2.5K | ~3.5K | ~4.5K | ~6K | ~7K |

**Ramp (Track B, base case):**
| Month | 3 | 6 | 9 | 12 | 18 | 24 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paid instances | 5 | 25 | 50 | 80 | 130 | 200 |
| Net | ~$0 | ~$0.5K | ~$1.5K | ~$2.5K | ~$4K | ~$6K |

Both land in the research's honest **$2–8K/mo in 12–24mo** band. Neither hits $10–25K in year one.

---

## 6. Go / No-Go gates (cheapest validation first)

- **Gate 0 (Day 14, ~$200):** Deal-flow + disqualifier scan. **NO-GO if** zero Track-A candidates
  AND zero Track-B tools survive the 4 filters. Cost to learn "no": ~$200 + ~10 hrs.
- **Gate 1 (Day 30, ~$500):** Pick a track (see §2). Requires *either* a verified-MRR acquisition
  candidate *or* ≥3 real paying pre-commitments (a charged card, not a survey). **STOP if neither.**
- **Gate 2 (Day 90):** Track A — MRR held ±5% through transition, on-call < 8 hrs/wk. Track B — ≥5
  paying instances, churn tolerable. **Pause & reassess vs CutLog if missed.**
- **Gate 3 (Month 9):** Track A — net ≥ $3K/mo and Hooman < 5 hrs/wk. Track B — ≥30 instances.
  **Kill and redirect to CutLog if missed.**

**Cheapest possible pre-money validation:** before ANY build/purchase money, get a **real card
charge** (Track B pre-order) or **verified Stripe payout evidence** (Track A). Surveys and
"would you pay" do not count.

---

## 7. Coexistence with CutLog (capital + delegation, NOT focus)

Master-report §5 is explicit: Hooman has time for **one** serious 0→1, and that is **CutLog**.
This plan respects that:

- **CutLog gets the focus hours; this gets capital.** Track A is chosen precisely because an
  acquired, already-running business demands *ops oversight*, not *0→1 hustle* — it can be run in
  < 5 hrs/wk once a contractor owns support/on-call.
- **The contractor is the coexistence mechanism.** Hire tier-1 support + on-call early (month 4
  Track A; ~$3K MRR Track B). Hooman is escalation-only. If the business can't fund the contractor
  from its own margin, that is the signal it's stealing focus from CutLog — pause it (Gate 3).
- **Hard rule:** if in any month this consumes > 10 hrs of Hooman's time OR CutLog progress
  visibly slips, this project pauses until a contractor absorbs the load. CutLog is never the
  variable that gives.
- **Track B is discouraged for exactly this reason** — it is a second distribution grind on
  Hooman's weakest axis and directly competes with CutLog for hours. Only pursue if Gate 1
  produces a rare validated niche and no acquisition is available.

---

## 8. Bottom line

Pursue this **only via acquisition (Track A)**, treating capital as the substitute for the
distribution muscle Hooman lacks and the hours CutLog already owns. Do not build a from-scratch
UniFi/n8n host. Gate every dollar behind verified paying demand. Plan to $2–8K/mo net in 12–24
months, delegated to a contractor, with CutLog remaining the primary venture. If Gate 0 or Gate 1
fails cheaply, walk away — the low downside is the whole reason this idea survived at all.
